flawed_step: Step 4: the assertion that three attachment vertices on a cycle must include two consecutive vertices is false.
counterexample: Inflate the Petersen graph: replace each vertex by a triangle whose three vertices correspond to its incident edges, and join corresponding triangle vertices for every Petersen edge. The resulting 30-vertex graph is 3-connected and claw-free but has no Hamiltonian cycle.
assessment_summary:
Attempted proof and audit:
1. Let G be an arbitrary 3-connected claw-free graph. Audit: JUSTIFIED — this is the standard starting point for proving the universal statement.
2. Choose a longest cycle C in G. Audit: JUSTIFIED — 3-connectivity implies minimum degree at least 3, hence G contains a cycle; finiteness supplies a longest one.
3. If C is not spanning, choose a component H of G−V(C); then H has at least three distinct neighbors on C. Audit: JUSTIFIED — otherwise deleting its at most two neighbors on C would disconnect H from the remaining vertices, contradicting 3-connectivity.
4. Since H has at least three attachment vertices on C, two of them are consecutive on C. Audit: NOT JUSTIFIED — three vertices on a cycle can be mutually separated; for example, alternate vertices of a 6-cycle are pairwise nonconsecutive, and claw-freeness has not supplied the missing conclusion.
5. For consecutive attachments x,y, connect suitable neighbors of x and y by a path through H and replace the edge xy of C by that path. Audit: CONDITIONALLY JUSTIFIED — if Step 4 supplied such x,y, connectedness of H would produce a simple path and the replacement would make a longer cycle, but Step 4 did not establish the premise.
6. This contradicts maximality of C, so C is spanning. Audit: NOT ESTABLISHED — the contradiction depends on the invalid Step 4.
7. Therefore C is a Hamiltonian cycle and G is Hamiltonian. Audit: CONDITIONALLY JUSTIFIED — a spanning cycle is Hamiltonian by definition, but spanning was not proved.

Independent verification that the statement is false:
8. Define the Petersen graph P with vertices a_i,b_i for i modulo 5 and edges a_i a_{i+1}, a_i b_i, and b_i b_{i+2}. Audit: JUSTIFIED — this defines a finite simple cubic connected graph; it is triangle-free because each of the two displayed layers is a 5-cycle and no mixed triangle is possible.
9. Deleting at most two edges from P leaves it connected. Audit: JUSTIFIED — if an edge cut of size d∈{1,2} existed, take its shore A with |A|≤5; cubicity gives 3|A|=2|E(P[A])|+d. For d=1, the possible odd sizes 1,3,5 would require respectively 1,4,7 internal edges, exceeding the triangle-free maxima 0,2,6. For d=2, sizes 2,4 would require 2,5 edges, exceeding the maxima 1,4.
10. Construct X by replacing every vertex v of P with a triangle T_v whose vertices correspond to the three edges incident with v, and for each edge uv of P join its corresponding vertices in T_u and T_v. Audit: JUSTIFIED — this unambiguously defines a finite simple undirected graph.
11. X is claw-free. Audit: JUSTIFIED — every vertex has three neighbors, and its two neighbors within its own triangle are adjacent, so its neighborhood cannot be the three independent leaves of an induced K_{1,3}.
12. X is 3-connected. Audit: JUSTIFIED — deleting at most two vertices removes at most two corresponding external edges; every residual T_v is a nonempty connected clique, and contracting these residual cliques yields P with at most two edges deleted, which is connected by Step 9.
13. If X had a Hamiltonian cycle D, contracting every T_v would produce a Hamiltonian cycle of P. Audit: JUSTIFIED — D crosses the three-edge cut around each T_v a positive even number of times, hence exactly twice; after contraction its external edges form a connected spanning 2-regular subgraph of P, which is a Hamiltonian cycle.
14. P has no Hamiltonian cycle. Audit: JUSTIFIED — such a cycle would use an even number k of the five spokes. It cannot use 0. If k=2, the two spoke indices must be adjacent on the outer 5-cycle but adjacent on the inner 5-cycle as well, requiring their difference to be both ±1 and ±2 modulo 5. If k=4, rotate indices so the unused spoke is a_0b_0; the degree requirements force the alleged cycle to split into the two cycles a_0a_1b_1b_4a_4a_0 and a_2a_3b_3b_0b_2a_2, so it is not one Hamiltonian cycle.
15. Consequently X is a 3-connected claw-free graph without a Hamiltonian cycle. Audit: JUSTIFIED — Steps 11–14 verify all required properties, so X refutes the statement.
